before.prompt: If Gold 2 moves into your new route, what could you do?

options.text: Change direction or stay as another support option
Insist on the return pass anyway

before.explanation: The pass does not obligate the receiver to return it; another support action may be better.

after.prompt: Before offering an inside option, which description matches the two gold defenders in this view?

options.text: Gold 1 is closer to F2; Gold 2 is farther toward the attacking net and nearer the middle
Gold 2 is closer to F2; Gold 1 is farther toward the attacking net and nearer the middle

after.explanation: Gold 1 is close to F2, while Gold 2 is farther toward Gold’s net and nearer the middle across the rink. Account for both the opponent near the carrier and the opponent in the inside space ahead of YOU. Their positions do not prove who will move, which line will stay available or whether F2 will return the puck.

revisionReason: Replaces unnecessary retreat with observation of the two actual defender relationships. No route or prior movement invented.

optionReasons.reason: Gold1 is closer to F2, Gold2 has greater attacking x and smaller |y|; all three comparisons agree with this frame. These are spatial cues, not claimed defensive assignments.
Reverses all three observed comparisons. Both named players are actual opponents, and this arrangement could exist elsewhere, but is not the shown setup.

geometry.method: Euclidean actor distances for stated player relationships; x advances toward attacked right net; |y| measures distance from middle across rink width. makeScene confirms current puck, though this question does not compare puck lanes.

duplicateAudit.distinction: q1 identifies F2 possession; q8 mentions Gold1 facing F2. This question compares Gold1/Gold2 locations, including Gold2 inside/up-ice position; it does not repeat possession, prescribe q4/q9 movement, or ask generic reoffer effectiveness from q6/q10.
